answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the cipher identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 138 runs and collects one. Because the karst index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the onyx audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 138 answers need 138 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
